Lessons.Title: Explore Multiplication Strategies with Rectangles
ExplanationParagraphs: A rectangle area is its rows multiplied by columns, counted in square units. Divide it into smaller non-overlapping rectangles, multiply their dimensions and add the subareas.

Original 2021 warm-up four diagrams visually inspected: 4×4 with two disjoint blue 2×2 corner patches has 8 shaded of16 total; 4×6 split horizontally into two2-row bands has24 total;3×6 with first five columns blue has15 blue plus3 white=18; complete3×6 has18.

Activity1 Andre finds area of3×6 as two3×3 parts:2×(3×3)=18. Elena's same3×6 rectangle is partitioned into5 plus1 column:3×(5+1)=(3×5)+(3×1)=15+3=18. Their methods differ in where they split the rectangle.

Activity1 another original grid is4×9=36. Pupils can invent different decompositions, for example4×(5+4)=20+16, and MUST shade a mathematically consistent partition. Original does not prescribe a unique answer.

Activity2 Noah marks a3×7 rectangle by5×3+2×3=21; Priya marks a4×6 rectangle as2×(2×6)=24; Tyler marks an8×8 rectangle as5×8+3×8=64. All three source diagrams and expressions were checked against original source SVGs.

Teacher checks groupings, dimensions, shading, absence of overlap and discussion; a bare numerical area does not satisfy the original representation tasks. Edulytics rectangles are new first-party drawings, not publisher paths. Cool-down Mark or Shade Parts to Find Area is gated.

KeyConcepts.Title: Rectangle area
KeyConcepts.Definition: Unit squares form rows and columns.

KeyConcepts.Title: Distributive area
KeyConcepts.Definition: Split a side into two lengths and add partial rectangular areas.

KeyConcepts.Title: Repeated half-regions
KeyConcepts.Definition: Associative grouping can double an equal partial area.
